> I believe moderation powers should be exclusive to group moderators in their instances, and instance owners in their private instances. The world creator should not have moderation powers in public instances, in other group's group public instances, or in other people's private instances. Basically, just remove the world creator moderation powers.

I'm not a world creator, but I would like to have this **not** changed! It's the world creators work and they should be able to do anything to there work/world they want to do. Just out of repect to respect there work i would like to have this not changed. As a group you are only guest you should get your own world if a world creator doesn't like you.

Why should world authors be forced to lose all control over the moderation of their world if toxic groups decide to set up shop and dominate the public instance list?

What can be done about that? Why should a world author be forced to serve those toxic groups with just hope that it will get better?

You mean removing previlegedes of somebody is shortsighted and toxic, right?

If not, It's shortsighted to believe that creators will continue there work if they don't have tools to protect there work. And it's toxic to remove there previledges in a personal fight where they are trying to protect ther work.

You are right it doesn't give them the right to be toxic but that's something else which needs to be decided by the T&S Team and also needs to be punished individually and not generally. That's something which doesn't require to remove everyones previledges on there work.

I don't see any reason why i should remove somebodies previledges only because "you" have an issue with them. If they don't like to show there work to "you" than what? Just go somewhere else and have a nice day.

I appreciate the support, but please don't get into fights. Let's all stay civilized and constructive with the comments here.

(EDIT: It looks like whoever this was a comment to deleted their comments or was removed from VRChat/Canny?)

@{60e65f577ae9d0492b0f2a75|full_name}: I guess my main reasoning is that there is a disconnect between what is and isn't public. If the world creator wants to keep total control over their work, then they shouldn't publish it for public use.

I can understand if the world creator is doing an event in a Public instance of their world and they want to moderate it. But then they could just use a Group Public instance instead, which not only give them more moderation controls, but also clearly tells everyone that this is an instance that is moderated by a group.

It is a fact that most VRChat players don't even know that world creators have these moderation powers over EVERY instance of their world.

@{58c6cbcffd04b1785f747b6c|full_name}: I don't understand your issue here. When you say "groups", are you talking about actual VRChat Groups, or just groups of players?

The obvious answer is: If an instance has toxic players, and muting/blocking them isn't enough, then those toxic players can be vote-kicked. If the toxic players are the majority in the instance, then you just make a new Public instance or even a Group Public instance where you can moderate it yourself. This is true for all of VRChat, no world creator/author moderator powers required.

What if the world creator/author is one of those toxic players? Then you are completely out of luck in Public instances of their world, since you literally cannot get rid of them without vote-kicking them. Your only choice is to make a VRChat Group, ban the world creator/author from the group, and make a Group Public instance.

@{60e65f577ae9d0492b0f2a75|full_name}: imma make this short and simple vrchat world creators are still bound by the guidelines(this includes group guidelines there is no super ceding this) regardless of world creation, if they become toxic its up to the group owner to forbid them from joining the group.if the world owner becomes a safety hazard for any groups that want there members to be in a safe space, doesnt matter at all if you break rules or abuse your world in any way people are going to refuse your access. that's how the vrchat system works.

For example, the furry talk and chill banning there users with their ban panel (violation of guidelines creating a similar blocklist system) using a discord server with every listed rulebreaker that have broke there world rules, is not allowed. because it violates the vrchat moderations system creating a dynamic blocklist.

the ban panel also works against group staff members(also against guidelines may not impersonate group moderators or group staff)  and may even get there world taken down if found to be abusing that panel system in group instances if there world is reported for such.

what i dont understand is why you guys think just because someone makes a world "for" vrchat, means they own the world when in fact that's not the truth vrchat owns your world because they could just up and take the world, and remove the world from you if they felt like it. if you dont want groups in your world dont make your world for vrchat make it for somewhere else.

so far all ive seen is rulebreakers and violations and nothing to fix any of this, just more rule breaking. then came along groups which fixed this issue and now people want to allow rule breakers by removing groups from ever accessing worlds. What goes through your head when you dont exactly think about the consequences.

heck the groups I've visited allow kids under the age of 13 to be in the lobbies and no staff or moderation team in the group is doing anything about it so my point exactly why even care. its not my group.

I don't expect VRChat to just simply remove this without replacing it with something else. But I seriously believe that the world creator moderation powers need to be removed.

Especially when you factor in all the huge arguments that it is already causing. World creators complaining about being kicked or banned from Group Public instances of their world, or world creators using moderator powers in another group's Group Public instance. This has the potential for moderation wars basically, with world creators arguing that they have the right to do whatever they want in instances of their world, and groups with Group Public instances being confused about why someone they didn't give permission is moderating their instances.

I have seen a few people suggest that a world creator should be able to set a VRChat Group as being official for a world, so that all normal public instances are automatically replaced with group public instances of that official group. I assume world creators would feel that is a fair replacement for the loss of their default moderation power.

@{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name}: Do you have a canny post for that idea so I can link to it?

@{58c6cbcffd04b1785f747b6c|full_name}: Also, what do you mean by the world creator/author being forced to serve them? The world is published and made public for everyone to use. It is literally against the creator guidelines to blacklist people from using a public world.

The world creator/author doesn't own the list of public instances, and they definitely shouldn't be attempting to moderate it. But if they want, they can make their own instance of the world and try to make it more popular than the instances they don't like. If those other instances are really so bad, then it won't be hard to make a more popular instance.

The normal players that use the world can do the same if they don't like the currently active public instances, they can just make a new instance. When making their own instance, they can then moderate it however they want, and preferably this is done with a Group Public instance so people that join know it will be moderated and by whom.

If the world creator/author doesn't want people to use a published world however they want, then they should unpublish/delete the world.

(I originally posted this elsewhere, but am gonna port it here too.)

VRChat has shown, through their [Creator Guidelines](https://hello.vrchat.com/creator-guidelines), that they don't want world creators to restrict access to their worlds or preemptively punish players for actions done outside of the current instance.

Through the implemention of groups, we can see that they don't want to have to rely on world creators to moderate public instances of their worlds.

These things are what makes me think I am on the right track for what VRChat is intending. Players can make a group public instance with their group of any published world they want and moderate it however they please. Players can choose to join the instance that has the level of moderation they prefer. And normal public instances are a mix between the wild west where there is no moderation at all, or a world creator's own varied moderation efforts.

I simply argue that new players to VRChat won't understand that some normal public instances can even have moderation. So I think this should be made clearer, for example have the world creator select a group to represent all normal public instances if they intend to be moderating their world, essentially replacing all normal public instances of that world with group public instances. That would allow players to more clearly know when a world is or isn't moderated.

To prevent the weird inconsistency, remove the world creator's moderation powers over all instances of their world. Many players don't even know they exist. And this will prevent the world creator from attempting to moderate an instance where they shouldn't have powers anyway. This would make it consistent and understandable by new players, that group public instances have moderation and normal public instances don't.

As an example of my reasoning, see **unexcept**'s comments here: [disable-group-instance-ability-to-kick-world-authors](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/disable-group-instance-ability-to-kick-world-authors)

Then just don't be annoying to world creators or give them a reason to moderate you lol. If I make a world and release it to the public I should have the right to moderate it how I see fit and remove people I don't want from my world.

@{621afb77c20d153ae60791a9|full_name}, I won't bring my personal drama in here, but trust me it can happen without you annoying a world creator. World creators are people too, some of them can be unreasonable and even malicious.

Sure, I have come to accept that in a normal Public instance, the world creator is the only one with moderation privilege. That works fine as a fallback and prevents those instances from being completely unmoderated.

However, if I make a Group Public instance with my personal group, I don't want the world creator to have moderation powers in my instance. Does this seem unreasonable to you? What about if I make a private Friends+ instance, is it ok that the world creator has moderation powers in that instance too?

A malicious world creator that has personal beef with some group can literally enter their Group Public instances and start to secretly moderate users in order to give the group a bad reputation or start infighting within the group. This can then lead to moderation wars, where world creators and group moderators fight to kick each other first.

The world creator can have moderation powers in the normal public instances, since they are otherwise unmoderated. But in any other instances they should definitely not have moderation powers. Instance owner should have more authority over their instance, not the the world creator.

@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name} If a world creator is being malicious than why even play their world if they're just gonna ban you guys secretly. If a world creator wants to do that and lose a bunch of players in the process that's ultimately up to them. Most world creators are pretty reasonable and if they're not then there's plenty of others who are.

@{621afb77c20d153ae60791a9|full_name}, Some worlds are just so niche that they don't have alternatives, or they are the only populated version of their type. So either we use those worlds and deal with the inconveniences, or we simply can't use those worlds.

This is most notable with game worlds, since they might require public instances and influx of new players. These are also the types of worlds where world creators seem more likely to try and enforce some form of moderation.

As for "banning", that is actually not allowed according to the Creator Guidelines. World creators are not allowed to programmatically prevent players from using their published worlds.

The only "banning" anyone is allowed to do, is with groups. You can ban users from your group and thereby prevent them from entering your group's instances. And this includes other users banning a world creator from their group if they don't want them around.

@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name}The real answer is that You shouldn't be using that world if you have a problem with its creator, chance is that you'll keep having issues with them and the changes their make to the world anyway.

@{60a61b373332241d8a817fb7|full_name}: Sadly it is a very niche game world, with barely any good alternatives. Not to talk too much drama, but when the world's creator then goes and directly attacks any worlds that tries to be an alternative, it kinda all becomes a little toxic. I and many others are addicted to the game in this world, so if we want to play it we often don't have a choice.

This is why I believe it would be a good idea for VRChat to limit the power of the world's creator, so they can actually see where the limit of their power is. If they didn't have moderation powers in Group Public instances owned by others, world creators would naturally stop trying to control those spaces.
@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name}I get that, but I don't see the issue, when I decide to boycott a studio/creator, that means that I also don't get to play the games they made.

@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name}It should be assumed that world creators have at the very least scripted themselves some kind of debugging backdoor. Given that I can already decide whether you're allowed to use items/drones or decals in my world, or hell, how fast you can move.
@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name}I forgot that ultimately world creators can unpublish their world, no questions asked.
I do not see a issue with this if anything I think world creators should have more powers.

@{66035290730e0be239bc91c3|full_name}, then we are simply of opposing opinions. And therefore I will now ban you from my super popular VRChat world for no other reason whatsoever. Anyway, jokes aside.

Why should a world creator be allowed to enter a group's instance and kick the group's owners/moderators?

What if a world creator enters your friends+ instance and kicks you? You would be ok with that?

A world creator can do whatever they want with normal public instances. No one really own those, and it can default to have the world creator as owner in that case. Though, I would rather see normal public instances replaced with group public instances owned by a group the world creator specify.

@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name}Then i guess you're gonna have to do without the niche. At the end of the day there is nothing you can do to prevent a world creator from removing access to their world. And then everyone lose everything.

@{60a61b373332241d8a817fb7|full_name}, you are right, if a world creator goes the scorched earth route, there is nothing anyone can do and everyone loses.

I admit that my stance on this issue has changed slightly over the years, but I still believe it would just be best for the health of VRChat's community if the question of "who has authority over an instance" was answered.

The easiest solution is to just remove the world creator's moderation powers over non-Public instances. This would make it clear to world creators that they don't have authority over individual instances that they don't own, and slowly shift the mentality of what they should and shouldn't be moderating.

details:
Currently if you are the creator of a world, you have moderation powers in all instances of that world. Most notably, you can kick people without a vote-to-kick. This is an old rule from before Groups were implemented in VRChat, and I believe it has become redundant now. Current world creator moderation powers:

- Has moderation powers in any instance of the world (even in private and group public instances)

- Can warn users

- Can force mic off

- Can kick users

- Can see people that blocked them on Here list

- Can see who started vote-kicks

If you incur the anger of a world's creator, they currently have the ability to simply kick you on sight from any instance of their world. And if the world creator is controlling enough, they can patrol all public instances and completely prevent you from using public instances of their world. If you happen to share the same friend groups, they can even join friends+ instances and kick you there too.

With the new [Creator Guidelines](https://hello.vrchat.com/community-guidelines), world creators are not allowed to automate blacklisting of people from their worlds using Udon scripts, and in-world moderators aren't allowed to punish people using udon moderation tools unless the they has broken rules in that instance. However there are no rules saying that a world creator can't just instant-kick those people on sight using the world creator moderation powers.

I believe moderation powers should be exclusive to group moderators in their instances, and instance owners in their private instances. The world creator should not have moderation powers in public instances, in other group's group public instances, or in other people's private instances. Basically, just remove the world creator moderation powers.

There are feature requests for the exact opposite point if view too. Some world creators want more control. But those feature requests has been said to be redundant now that group public instances exist. See: [moderation-tools-for-world-creators](https://vrchat.canny.io/feature-requests/p/moderation-tools-for-world-creators), and: [allow-world-creators-to-prevent-groups-of-creating-group-instances-on-their-worl](https://vrchat.canny.io/feature-requests/p/allow-world-creators-to-prevent-groups-of-creating-group-instances-on-their-worl)
title: Remove World Creator Moderation Powers
